title: Finite components of strict open reduction on K-flat representatives
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, independent scheme and coefficient universes, an open immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow V$, its coefficient transports and exact open operations $o$, two reduction calculi $S_V,S_X$, a generator-normalized ordinary open tensor comparison $\theta$, and a strict comparison $r$ [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison, def-trf-compact-support-system-evaluation-diagram]. Let $Q$ be an unbounded flat-term K-flat complex of completed coefficient modules on $X$, with $\mathbf Q(Q)$ derived complete [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-weil-derived-complete]. Write $JQ$ for its termwise open extension. There is a proof of K-flatness of $JQ$ such that, for every positive coefficient level $n+1$, the evaluated comparison $\alpha_n$ equals the following explicitly constructed isomorphism $\beta_n(Q)$: apply finite reduction to the exact-localization isomorphism $j_!\mathbf Q(Q)\cong\mathbf Q(JQ)$; apply the K-flat finite-reduction model of $JQ$; localize the degreewise ordinary isomorphism $\theta_n$; invert the exact-localization isomorphism for finite open extension on the tensor complex of $Q$; finally apply finite open extension to the inverse K-flat finite-reduction model of $Q$. Here $\alpha_n$ is evaluation of $r$ followed and preceded by the recorded reduction-evaluation and exact open-evaluation isomorphisms. This asserts an equality of whole isomorphisms at each finite level, with no claim about a quotient arrow.

proof.text: Apply r.strictModel to the given flat-term K-flat Q and its completeness. Retain its K-flatness witness for the extension, its representative isomorphisms, and its single chain comparison.

Evaluate the whole-system representative equation. The first identities of the two CoefficientReductionPresentation predicates give the precise reductionEvaluation followed by coefficientFiniteReductionModel. The degreewise finite-component equation is an equality of cochain morphisms.

Use the exact-functor localization factor formula for the ordinary extension-evaluation square, proved by the compositor and natural-isomorphism factor identities. Apply derived finite evaluation to the strict representative equation. Naturality moves the extension and evaluation factors; the degreewise component identity replaces the localized chain comparison. The two presentation identities and naturality of reductionEvaluation identify the two sides. Cancel the source reduction-evaluation isomorphism and the target finite model and exact-localization factors, then use isomorphism extensionality.
